jobs.description:
Job Description

Title:
Director, Finance (CSM)

Id:
21596

Type:
FullTime

Location:
Bolton, ON

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

Husky TechnologiesTM is committed to developing inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If contacted in relation to a job opportunity or testing, you should advise the member of the Talent Acquisition team in a timely fashion of any disabilities that requires accommodation measures in order to enable you to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner.

Information received relating to accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.

No agency or telephone inquiries please.

jobs.description:

About the Opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Finance executive to help lead a significant organizational transformation within a large, complex public sector institution. As Executive Director, Integrated Finance Services, you'll play a pivotal role in launching a new service delivery model, bringing together Finance teams, strengthening partnerships and creating a more consistent, responsive approach to financial services.
This role calls for more than technical Finance expertise. You'll be a visible, empathetic leader who can navigate change, build trust with senior stakeholders and create a strong sense of team identity. You'll balance strategic oversight with hands-on execution, ensuring the new operating model delivers meaningful results for the people and departments it supports.

What's In It for You

• An opportunity to operationalize a significant Finance transformation with institution-wide impact.
• A collaborative environment where relationship-building, thoughtful leadership and continuous improvement are valued.
• The chance to develop high-performing leaders, influence executive decisions and build a service-oriented team culture.
• An exceptional and competitive total rewards package, including comprehensive health and wellness benefits, free day care for families, education reimbursement for immediate family members, and a generous pension plan designed to support your long-term financial well-being.
• Relocation reimbursement support may be provided on a case-by-case basis

Your Responsibilities

• You'll lead the implementation and continuous improvement of an integrated Finance operating model, translating strategic priorities into effective service delivery across multiple portfolios.
• You'll oversee Finance Directors and their teams, establishing clear accountability, service standards, governance frameworks, performance measures and escalation protocols.
• You'll monitor service quality, responsiveness, operational capacity and client outcomes, identifying systemic challenges and driving timely corrective action.
• You'll oversee cross-portfolio resource planning, workload distribution and capacity management, balancing competing priorities and addressing organizational risks.
• You'll provide executive-level advice on financial performance, institutional budgeting, forecasting, reporting, internal controls and emerging financial or operational risks.
• You'll build trusted relationships with senior academic and administrative leaders, navigating sensitive stakeholder dynamics, influencing decisions and strengthening confidence in Finance services.
• You'll coach, mentor and develop senior Finance leaders, fostering accountability, succession planning, collaboration and a strong, service-focused team culture.
• You'll lead the implementation of Finance transformation initiatives, process standardization, automation and enterprise systems improvements, ensuring successful adoption and measurable benefits.
• You'll champion continuous improvement through service reviews, performance data, stakeholder feedback and risk assessments, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and effectiveness.

Skills and Qualifications

• 10+ years of progressive senior Finance leadership experience within a large, complex organization, including oversight of multiple Finance functions and leadership through Directors or senior managers.
• University degree in Finance, Accounting, Commerce, Business Administration or a related field, along with a CPA or equivalent recognized professional accounting designation.
• Extensive expertise in institutional budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, enterprise reporting, financial controls, risk management and complex funding or revenue structures.
• Proven experience implementing large-scale Finance transformations, shared services or integrated operating models, including service governance, performance frameworks and organizational change.
• Strong understanding of enterprise Finance systems, process automation and technology-enabled improvements, with the ability to assess implementation effectiveness and operational impact.
• Demonstrated success advising and influencing executive stakeholders, building consensus across diverse business units and navigating complex organizational environments.
• Proven ability to lead and develop high-performing management teams, establish clear performance expectations, manage organizational capacity and foster an inclusive, collaborative culture.
• Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify systemic risks, balance competing priorities and translate strategy into operational results.
• Strong relationship-building, communication and change leadership skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively, navigate resistance and lead with empathy.
• Experience within post-secondary education, healthcare, government, research-intensive institutions or similarly complex, multi-stakeholder organizations is strongly preferred.

Why Partner with Altis

If you’ve never worked with a staffing agency before, we make it easy. We work with top employers across Canada who have great jobs to fill, each vetted and verified by our team. When you apply for a job with Altis, we get to know you as a candidate and learn what your strengths are. Then, if you’re a solid match, we handle all the logistics, advocating for you as a candidate for the role, providing access to coaching and connecting you directly with the hiring manager. And rest assured, all our services are free of cost for candidates.

Since 1878, Western University has been committed to serving our communities through the pursuit of academic excellence and by providing students, faculty, and community members with life-long opportunities for intellectual, social, and cultural growth. We seek excellent students, faculty, and staff to join us in what has become known as the "Western Experience" - an opportunity to contribute to a better world through the development of new knowledge, new abilities, new connections, and new ways to make a difference.

The Senior Director provides strategic oversight and leadership to the Faculty's administrative functions and senior administrative leaders, establishes integrated planning and governance frameworks, and advises the Dean and Faculty leadership on significant resource, organizational, operational and risk decisions. jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Industrial Minerals and Fertilizer Production
Location: Saskatoon, Saskatchewan (in-office)
Reports To: Vice President
Position Type: Full-Time, Executive Leadership
Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is responsible for the financial management, strategy, and performance of the Company, an industrial minerals and fertilizer producer with mining, mineral processing, manufacturing, and distribution operations.

As a key member of the executive leadership team, the CFO will oversee financial reporting, accounting, treasury, taxation, budgeting, forecasting, financing, and risk management. The CFO will also provide financial leadership for major capital projects, operational improvements, and strategic growth initiatives.

The successful candidate will combine strong financial and commercial judgment with an understanding of capital-intensive industrial operations, manufacturing economics, and commodity markets.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy and Leadership

Develop and execute the Company's financial strategy in support of its operational and long-term business objectives.
Advise executive management and the Board of Directors on financial performance, capital allocation, business risks, and strategic opportunities.
Provide financial leadership in major business decisions, investments, acquisitions, and strategic initiatives.
Support corporate governance, Board reporting, and shareholder communications.

2. Financial Reporting and Controls

Oversee corporate accounting, consolidated financial reporting, taxation, and financial systems, coordinating with the accounting teams at both plant locations.
Ensure timely and accurate financial statements in accordance with applicable accounting standards.
Maintain effective financial policies, internal controls, and reporting procedures.
Manage external audits and relationships with auditors, tax advisors, and other professional service providers.
Ensure compliance with applicable financial, tax, and regulatory requirements.

3. Treasury and Corporate Financing

Manage liquidity, cash flow, working capital, and capital structure.
Maintain relationships with banks, lenders, shareholders, and other capital providers.
Negotiate and administer credit facilities, debt financing, and other funding arrangements.
Monitor financial covenants and lender reporting requirements.
Oversee financial risk exposures, including foreign exchange, interest rates, and commodity-related risks.

4. Financial Planning and Performance Management

Lead annual operating and capital budgets, financial forecasts, and long-term financial planning.
Monitor financial performance against budgets and operating plans.
Analyze profitability, production costs, operating margins, and working capital performance.
Establish financial and operational performance indicators to support management decisions.
Work with operations and commercial management to identify opportunities for improved profitability and cost efficiency.

5. Oversight of Plant Finance and Accounting

Provide financial leadership and oversight to professional accounting staff at the Company's two plant locations.
Ensure plant accounting teams maintain responsibility for day-to-day accounting, financial reporting, cost accounting, and financial controls.
Establish consistent financial policies, reporting standards, and procedures across both facilities.
Coordinate with plant accounting personnel on budgets, forecasts, financial performance, and operational cost analysis.
Support plant accounting teams in maintaining effective financial management, accountability, and alignment with corporate financial objectives.

6. Capital Projects and Project Financing

Provide financial oversight of major capital projects, including plant expansions and new production facilities.
Evaluate project economics, financial returns, and investment risks.
Monitor capital budgets, project costs, forecasts, and cash flow requirements.
Support project financing, lender due diligence, and government funding applications.
Ensure appropriate financial controls and reporting throughout project development and construction.

7. Commercial and Operational Support

Provide financial analysis to support product pricing, customer profitability, and commercial decisions.
Evaluate the financial implications of procurement, transportation, distribution, and supply chain arrangements.
Support negotiations involving major customers, suppliers, and service providers.
Monitor customer credit exposure and commercial financial risks.

8. Leadership and Organizational Development

Lead the corporate finance function and provide financial leadership and support to professional accounting personnel at both plant locations.
Establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and accountability.
Improve financial systems, reporting capabilities, and business processes.
Promote collaboration between finance, operations, commercial, and executive management.

Qualifications and Experience

Required Qualifications

Professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).
Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related discipline.
Minimum 15 years of progressive financial management experience, including senior leadership responsibilities.
Experience as a CFO, Vice President Finance, Finance Director, or equivalent senior financial executive.
Experience in manufacturing, mining, mineral processing, chemicals, fertilizers, or another capital-intensive industrial sector.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, taxation, treasury, internal controls, and corporate financing.
Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and capital management.
Experience providing financial oversight of major capital projects.
Proven leadership and team development capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in the fertilizer, industrial minerals, potash, or specialty chemicals industries.
Familiarity with Canadian and U.S. markets and cross-border business operations.
Experience with project financing, government funding programs, and industrial construction projects.
Experience with mergers, acquisitions, and corporate restructuring.
Knowledge of mining royalties, environmental liabilities, and asset retirement obligations.
Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing cost accounting.

Key Competencies

Strategic and Commercial Judgment: Ability to evaluate financial and business opportunities and support sound management decisions.

Operational Understanding: Appreciation of manufacturing economics, production costs, capital investment, and supply chain management.

Financial Management: Strong capabilities in cash flow management, financial controls, financing, and financial planning.

Leadership: Ability to develop effective teams and work collaboratively across the organization.

Communication: Ability to present financial information clearly to management, the Board, shareholders, and lenders.

Execution and Accountability: Practical, results-oriented approach with strong organizational and problem-solving skills.

Key Performance Expectations

The CFO will be expected to:

Maintain adequate liquidity and a sustainable capital structure.
Deliver accurate, timely, and meaningful financial reporting.
Support achievement of profitability, cash flow, and working capital objectives.
Maintain effective financial controls and regulatory compliance.
Provide financial oversight of major capital investments and financing initiatives.
Develop an effective finance organization that supports operations and future growth.

Position Profile

The ideal candidate is a commercially minded, hands-on financial executive with experience in capital-intensive industrial operations.

The CFO will be expected to balance financial stewardship with strategic business support, working closely with executive management, plant accounting personnel, and commercial teams to improve financial performance, manage risk, and support profitable growth.

jobs.title: Director, Business Advisory & Succession Planning
jobs.description:
Under the direction of the Vice President & Head of Business Advisory and Succession Planning, the Director, Business Advisory and Succession Planning is part of a team of Subject Matter Experts (the “SME Team”) within BMO Private Wealth. As a member of the SME Team, you’ll join a team of diverse, highly accredited and experienced accountants, lawyers and business valuation subject matter experts.

The SME Team provides business advisory and succession planning services to high and ultra-high net worth (“HNW”) business owner clients to support the growth and retention of HNW client assets through specialized planning solutions that help to broaden the dialogue and enhance the client relationship in order to consolidate client assets and increase revenues with BMO Private Banking, BMO Nesbitt Burns or BMO Commercial advisors (the “BMO Advisors”).

A critical objective for this role is the enhancement of the BMO Advisors and Clients’ Experience, thus driving increased profitability, improved market share and Net Promotor Scores.

Key Accountabilities:

Provide customized business advisory and succession planning strategies and advice to the HNW client segments.
Act as a subject matter expert in the areas of business valuation and succession planning to properly assess and provide tailored insights and solutions to clients.
Provides guidance and strategies on the topics of business valuation, mergers and acquisitions, sale, growth, family transition and succession related events.
Leverage specialized knowledge and expertise to partner collaboratively with other planning professionals and BMO Advisors.
Demonstrates a consultative and collaborative value-added approach in client conversations, acting as a member of a client strategy team to facilitate the desired client experience and to achieve business goals.
Develop content in the areas of business succession and business owner planning for use as training or marketing materials, internal resource material and client facing material.
Act as a subject matter expert spokesperson on business succession planning both internally and externally to position BMO as a leader in wealth planning services; includes presentations and seminars within BMO and to clients.
Develop proactive, integrated, and customized strategies to help clients achieve their business, financial and personal goal.
Apply well-developed consultative sales and wealth planning principles, practices and techniques in client interactions.
Lead the development of educational programs in the areas of business succession and business owner planning.
Provide commentary and awareness on emerging business succession planning trends relevant to business owners, such as mergers & acquisition, business valuation, taxation, estate and trust planning, sound business and family governance and philanthropy.
Promote the services of the wealth planning and specialized planning professionals to BMO Advisors and other user groups.
Provide BMO Advisors and clients with accurate and detailed subject matter expertise in all areas of business owner advisory and succession planning.
Serve as in-house expert in providing business owner succession planning.
Where appropriate, partner with other planning specialists at BMO (e.g., Financial Planning Specialists, Will & Estate Consultants, Tax Specialists, Trust and Insurance Specialists, Mid-Market Mergers & Acquisitions, etc.)
Apply expertise and think creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non-routine.
Develop/maintain internal and external networks and referral sources to ensure ongoing growth of the business.
Partner with all members of BMO Private Wealth and Commercial Banking to provide a broad-based solutions approach for specific client situations.
Consult with clients and their external advisors on complex business succession planning issues, as required.
Operate at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a specialist resource to senior leaders and stakeholders.
Proactively spot, anchor, introduce and follow up on opportunities for complimentary businesses and solutions.
Assist BMO Advisors with business development, opportunity spotting, and revenue generation.
Lead, motivate and develop relationships with internal and external business partners / stakeholders to develop productive working relationships.
Protect the Bank’s assets by adhering to all banking, investment and lending regulations, Bank policies and procedures, legal and ethical requirements and regulations, process requirements, and established risk guidelines.

Qualifications:

Knowledge

University degree with business orientation (business, finance, accounting, law).
Relevant professional designation(s) (CPA, CBV, CFA, FEA, Bar Association) considered an asset.
Practiced in the field of corporate finance and business succession / valuation with a consulting firm and/or held a similar role at another financial institution.
A minimum of 10 years of experience providing valuation and succession planning advice to HNW business owners at a senior level.
Extensive knowledge and technical proficiency.
Experience working in a team of professionals with deep subject matter expertise.
Seasoned professional with a combination of education, experience and industry knowledge.
Extensive knowledge and technical proficiency in the areas of business valuation, mergers & acquisitions, and succession planning.
Knowledge of tax, estate and trust planning, insurance and philanthropy considered an asset.

Skills

Experienced, highly integrated and confident in dealing with the HNW private client segment.
Fluent in French and English - Strong communication and presentation skills; both written and verbal. Ability to communicate in a professional and authoritative manner.
Strong interpersonal skills, flexible and empathetic, self-starter, able to work effectively in a variety of situations in a team-oriented environment.
Ability to communicate complex information in a comprehensive and practical manner, including a strong understanding of client needs and expectations.
Collaboration & team skills; with a focus on cross-group collaboration.
Motivated with an entrepreneurial mindset.
Strong listening, analytical and problem-solving capabilities; strong consultative selling skills.
Strong team player with solid interpersonal and leadership skills.
Ability to think strategically and simultaneously resolve a magnitude of diverse, complex and ambiguous issues/situations in a creative and practical manner.
Strong prioritization, time management and multi-tasking skills.
Strong presentation and relationship management skills.
Flexible and empathetic, able to work effectively in various situations.
Strong work ethic, work well under pressure.

Customer service focus.
Teamwork, innovation and growth.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Financial Services, Private Capital
jobs.description:
The opportunity

Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board (Ontario Teachers') is a global investor with net assets of ~$279 billion as of December 31, 2025. Ontario Teachers’ is a fully funded defined benefit pension plan, and it invests in a broad array of asset classes to deliver retirement security for 346,000 working members and pensioners. Our Private Capital group deploys ~$60 billion across direct private equity investments and private equity funds globally.

The Managing Director will lead investments end-to-end — from origination through exit — sponsor transactions at Underwriting Committee, take active board roles at portfolio companies, and help build and develop the Financial Services investment team. This is a senior seat for a candidate with a proven private equity track record and deep Financial Services expertise.

Who You'll Work With

Reporting to the Senior Managing Director, the role will be part of a deal team comprising analysts, associates, principals, directors, and managing directors, supported by third-party consultants, operating executives, and legal and accounting advisors dedicated to each transaction.

The Financial Services team invests across sub-sectors including Insurance, Wealth & Asset Management, Lending, Professional Services, and Cards & Payments, with particular need to understand the regulatory, AI, and digitization themes reshaping the sector. The role will also potentially partner with colleagues in OTPP's global offices on international investment and / or cross asset class opportunities in Financial Services.

What You'll Do

Lead deal teams end-to-end, from origination through close and through the life of the investment; serve as the named sponsor at Underwriting Committee and author Underwriting Committee papers.
Own deal execution with limited oversight — including pricing, structuring, financing, and final commercial and legal negotiating positions.
Take active board leadership roles at portfolio companies; drive value creation agendas with management and sponsor follow-on capital, M&A, and exit decisions.

jobs.title: Chief Strategy & Enrolment Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Strategy & Enrolment Officer

Glenlyon Norfolk School | Victoria, British Columbia

An exceptional opportunity to shape the future of one of Canada's leading independent schools.

Glenlyon Norfolk School (GNS) is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking and entrepreneurial leader to join our Senior Leadership Team as our Chief Strategy and Enrolment Officer (CSEO).

This is more than an admissions leadership position. It is an opportunity for an exceptional strategist, relationship builder and organizational leader to help shape the future of GNS, strengthen our position in an evolving educational landscape and advance our long-term strategic priorities.

We are looking for someone who brings fresh perspectives, entrepreneurial thinking, demonstrated leadership and a genuine passion for education. Someone who sees opportunities where others see challenges, understands the importance of exceptional relationships and knows how to translate ambitious ideas into measurable results.

About Glenlyon Norfolk School

Established in 1913, GNS is a co-educational, not-for-profit International Baccalaureate (IB) World Continuum School serving students from Junior Kindergarten through Grade 12 on two beautiful campuses in Victoria, British Columbia.

We provide an exceptional educational experience for students, emphasizing robust academics, healthy social and emotional development, and inquiry-based, student-centred learning within a supportive community. Grounded in our five core values—Truth, Courage, Caring, Individuality and Community—we are committed to empowering students to do their best through truth and courage in learning and in life.

Guided by our Momentum strategic directions, GNS is entering an exciting chapter of innovation and growth. With distinctive day and boarding programs, personalized learning pathways and ambitious campus renewal plans, we are building on a strong foundation to shape the school's future.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the Head of School. the CSEO will provide executive leadership in advancing a comprehensive, data-informed enrolment strategy that strengthens demand, expands our reach and supports the long-term sustainability of GNS.

Working collaboratively across the school, you will:

Lead strategic growth: Develop and execute a multi-year enrolment strategy, identify emerging opportunities and strengthen GNS's competitive position across domestic, international and boarding markets.

Elevate the family experience: Champion a personalized, relationship-centred approach to admissions, engagement and retention that fosters meaningful and lasting connections with families.

Drive informed decision-making: Leverage market intelligence, financial insights and performance data to guide strategic priorities, enrolment planning and organizational growth.

Strengthen institutional partnerships: Collaborate with academic and operational leaders, Marketing and Communications, and Advancement to align enrolment priorities with the school's broader strategic direction.

Inspire high performance: Lead and develop a talented Admissions team, fostering innovation, collaboration, accountability and a commitment to exceptional service.

As a trusted strategic partner to the Head of School and an active member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will help influence decisions that extend beyond enrolment and contribute to the overall success of GNS. Working closely with Advancement and Marketing and Communications, you will strengthen strategic alignment across these functions, recognizing the important connections between enrolment, reputation, philanthropy and community engagement.

As GNS continues to evolve, this role offers the potential to contribute to a broader, more integrated approach to institutional strategy and advancement. We are seeking a leader who is energized by this opportunity and brings the vision, adaptability and ambition to grow alongside the school and help shape its future.

What We're Looking For
We are seeking an accomplished and engaging executive who combines strategic vision and commercial acumen with exceptional interpersonal skills, sound judgment and a genuine passion for education.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant progressive senior leadership experience in enrolment management, strategic growth, business development, marketing, constituent engagement or a related field, with demonstrated success delivering measurable results.

Proven ability to develop and execute strategies, identify growth opportunities and translate complex financial and market information into informed decisions.

Exceptional relationship-building, communication and influencing skills, complemented by personal warmth, authenticity and emotional intelligence.

A collaborative and empowering leadership style, with a track record of developing high-performing teams, leading change and building strong organizational partnerships.

A degree in a relevant discipline or an equivalent combination of education and senior leadership experience.

Experience in independent schools, post-secondary education or other mission-driven organizations is valued. A background in teaching, advancement, marketing and communications, familiarity with the IB, and/or international recruitment or boarding programs would also be considered an asset, but is not essential.

We welcome candidates who bring fresh perspectives, transferable expertise and the ability to balance ambitious strategic thinking with thoughtful, results-oriented execution.

To learn more about the full scope of this executive opportunity, please review the Chief Strategy and Enrolment Officer Job Description.

Why Join GNS?
This is an opportunity to make a meaningful and lasting contribution to a highly regarded independent school at an exciting stage in its development. You will work alongside a collaborative and committed leadership team, influence strategic decisions and help shape the future of a vibrant school community.

GNS offers a competitive total compensation package, including comprehensive health benefits, a health spending account, virtual health care, a generous RRSP program, tuition discounts, wellness programs and access to our fitness centre.

Located on beautiful Vancouver Island, Victoria offers an exceptional quality of life in one of Canada's most desirable coastal communities.

How to Apply
We invite qualified candidates to submit a letter of interest and detailed résumé by November 20, 2026. However, this position will remain open until filled.

Salary range: $140,000 - $165,000

Anticipated start date: Flexible, no later than summer 2027.

For more information about GNS, visit www.mygns.ca.

Glenlyon Norfolk School is committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive and welcoming community. We encourage applications from qualified individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process.

Personal information collected through the recruitment process will be treated confidentially and used only for recruitment purposes.
